nodes.question: When was the soil sampling conducted?
nodes.answer: The soil sampling was conducted in late summer of 2022.
nodes.paragraph: The soil is regularly ploughed to a depth of 30 cm and labelled as cropland in the following. The second soil was sampled from a grassland research station in Gie en and referred to as grassland (latitude N50 32 , longitude E8 41 , elevation 172 m a.s.l.). The soil was a flu - vic Gleysol with a clay loam texture, soil organic carbon contents of 4.42% and a pH of 6.71. The soil organic matter (SOM) content of the grassland soil was higher (4.46%) and the bulk density lower (1.0 g cm-3) compared to the cropland soil with SOC contents of 1.21% and a bulk density of 1.3 g cm-3, respectively (Rohe et al. 2021 ). More details about the field site can be found in Rohe et al. ( 2021 ). During sampling in late summer of 2022, a custom-made drill for undisturbed sampling of cylindrical soil cores (UGT GmbH, Germany) was used to take undisturbed samples (encased in a stiff 5 mm PE sleeve, Fig. 1). On each field site, five undis - turbed cores (10 cm height, 10 cm ) were taken from 5 to 15 cm depth.

nodes.question: How has X-ray microtomography been used in relation to soil?
nodes.answer: X-ray microtomography has been used to determine the volume fraction and distribution of air-filled pores in soil to help predict N2O emissions.
nodes.paragraph: As a consequence, the diffusion distances of dissolved oxy - gen through the wet soil matrix can be very different depend- ing on the soil management (see the case study on plowed cropland soil and no-till grassland soil below) (Lucas et al. 2023a ; Schl ter et al. 2020 ). X-ray microtomography has been used repeatedly as a means of determining the volume fraction and distribution of air-filled pores to help predicting N2O emissions (Lucas et al. 2023a; Porre et al. 2016; Rabot et al. 2015; Rohe et al. 2021). Particulate organic matter (POM) is also not randomly distributed within the soil matrix, but can be thoroughly mixed into the wet soil matrix or mainly located in air-filled macropores, depending on soil structure formation. Conceptual ideas on how the anaerobic soil volume is modulated by soil structure heterogeneity are few and have not yet been implemented in common ecosystem models. Here, we review the recent advances in the quantifica- tion of the anaerobic soil volume fraction using various experimental approaches and synthesize some pertinent relationships of the anaerobic soil volume with more read- ily available state variables through an extensive literature review. We conducted meta-analyses focusing on i) the critical air distances in soil leading to the formation of anoxia and ii) the anaerobic soil volume fraction estimated from oxic and anoxic incubations. Based on the results, we propose a new concept for including denitrification in process models operating at relevant scales such as that of a soil profile. As a result of spatial heterogeneity of organic carbon, oxygen and nitrate, denitrification is observed even under relatively dry conditions. However, it is unclear whether denitrifica - tion potentials of microbial communities exhibit spatial patterns relative to variations in distance to soil pores facilitating oxygen exchange and nutrient transfer. Thus, we determined genetic and process-level denitrification potentials in two contrasting soils, a cropland and a grassland, with respect to the distance to air-filled pores. An X-ray computed tomog - raphy aided sampling strategy was applied for precise sampling of soil material.

The primary objectives of this study were to examine the process-level denitrification potential in areas close to and distant from well-aerated pores along with assess - ing the local genetic denitrification potential. The goal was to determine whether the existing microbial communities, under ideal conditions for denitrification, exhibit compara - ble denitrification capabilities regardless of their proximity to pores. If this was true, then the capacity of the microbial community to denitrify does not have to be made spatially- explicit with respect to pore distances for modeling denitri - fication. We collected microsamples from two distinct soil sites, both near and far from visible pores based on X-ray CT scans. These samples were subjected to short-term anoxic incubations with optimal conditions for denitrification. nodes.question: Which elements were measured in the soil at the Swift Current site?
nodes.answer: The elements measured in the soil at the Swift Current site include bulk density, organic carbon, mineral nitrogen, and Olsen phosphorus.
nodes.paragraph: The same study was repeated from 2011 to 2018 at the Crop Diversification Centre, Brooks (50 33 N; 111 53 W; elevation: 747m), Alberta, Canada. Both sites are located in the Mixed Grassland Ecoregion of Canada, in an area where Brown Chernozem soils are prevalent. The soil (0 15 cm) at Swift Current is a silt loam, with 31% sand, 51% silt, and 18% clay, whereas at Brooks the soil (0 15 cm) is a sandy loam, with 46% sand, 32% silt, and 22% clay. At the initiation of this study, soil in the 0 15 cm layer at the Swift Current site had a pH (1:2 ratio of soil to water) of 6.5, bulk density of 1.3 g cm 3, organic carbon (dry combustion after removing inorganic using 6 M HCI) of 10.6 g kg 1, mineral N (2 M KCI extractable N) of 3.4 mg kg 1, and Olsen P (0.5 M NaHCO3) of 26.5 mg kg 1.
